attractions.name: Serengeti National Park
attractions.desc: The Serengeti's open grasslands host the largest overland mammal migration on Earth, with over a million wildebeest and zebra moving in a constant circuit between Tanzania and Kenya. Game drives here rank among the most reliable anywhere for spotting lions, cheetahs, and leopards. The scale of the landscape, flat and horizon-wide, is part of the experience itself.

attractions.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
attractions.desc: Africa's tallest peak rises alone from the surrounding plains, its snowy summit visible from great distances despite sitting almost on the equator. Several multi-day routes climb through five distinct ecological zones before reaching Uhuru Peak. No technical climbing skill is required, but altitude makes the final push genuinely demanding.

attractions.name: Ngorongoro Crater
attractions.desc: A collapsed volcanic caldera forms a natural enclosure packed with wildlife, including one of the region's few remaining black rhino populations. The crater floor stays green even in dry season, drawing animals down from the highlands. Descending the crater walls by vehicle feels like entering a self-contained ecosystem.

attractions.name: Zanzibar's Stone Town
attractions.desc: This old trading port on Zanzibar island mixes Arab, Persian, Indian, and European architecture along narrow, shaded lanes. Carved wooden doors and spice markets recall its centuries as a hub of the Indian Ocean trade. It pairs naturally with the white sand beaches found elsewhere on the island.

attractions.name: Tarangire National Park
attractions.desc: Known for its baobab-studded landscape and large elephant herds that gather along the Tarangire River during the dry season. It's quieter than the Serengeti but still delivers dense wildlife viewing, particularly for elephants and birdlife. Many visitors add it as a shorter stop before or after the bigger parks.

attractions.name: Lake Manyara
attractions.desc: A compact park set beneath the Rift Valley escarpment, known for tree-climbing lions and large flocks of flamingos along the alkaline lake shore. The dense groundwater forest gives way quickly to open lakeshore, packing varied scenery into a small area. It's often visited as a warm-up before the Serengeti.

itinerary.label: Days 1–2
itinerary.title: Arusha & Tarangire
itinerary.desc: Acclimatize in Arusha before a first game drive among Tarangire's baobabs and elephant herds.
itinerary.cost: Tarangire National Park entry costs about $60/day for non-residents, typically bundled into safari packages.
itinerary.food: Most safari camps include full board; expect hearty, simple meals designed around early game-drive schedules.

itinerary.label: Day 3
itinerary.title: Lake Manyara
itinerary.desc: A shorter park visit known for tree-climbing lions and flamingo flocks.
itinerary.cost: Park entry costs about $50/day for non-residents.
itinerary.food: Same as elsewhere on safari — meals are typically included with your lodge or camp.

itinerary.label: Days 4–5
itinerary.title: Ngorongoro Crater
itinerary.desc: Descend into the crater for dense wildlife viewing across a self-contained ecosystem.
itinerary.cost: Crater entry and conservation fees run about $70–80/day for non-residents, among the highest in the region.
itinerary.food: A packed lunch inside the crater is standard, since most lodges sit on the rim.

itinerary.label: Days 6–7
itinerary.title: Serengeti
itinerary.desc: Extended game drives across the plains, timed to the migration if possible.
itinerary.cost: Park entry costs about $70/day for non-residents.
itinerary.food: Timing meals around game drives is normal here — many camps offer flexible bush breakfasts and lunches.

itinerary.label: Days 8–9
itinerary.title: Zanzibar
itinerary.desc: Fly out to the coast for Stone Town and beach time to close the trip.
itinerary.cost: Stone Town's guided walking tours cost about $15–20; spice farm tours run $15–25.
itinerary.food: Try Zanzibar pizza from a Stone Town street stall in the evening — a genuine only-here specialty.

goodToKnow.tipping: USD 15–20/day for safari guides and drivers is standard
goodToKnow.safety: Safaris are well organized through established operators; Zanzibar's Stone Town is safe to walk by day
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Small-plane transfers connect the northern circuit parks quickly; roads between them are long and rough
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) is the main gateway for the northern safari circuit; Zanzibar has its own airport (ZNZ) for the coastal leg

food.name: Ugali
food.desc: A firm maize porridge that forms the starchy base of most everyday Tanzanian meals.

food.name: Nyama choma
food.desc: Charcoal-grilled meat, usually goat or beef, a staple of casual social eating.

food.name: Zanzibar pizza
food.desc: A street-food specialty from Stone Town: a thin dough stuffed with meat, egg, and vegetables, then fried.

food.name: Pilau
food.desc: Spiced rice cooked with meat and warming spices, showing Zanzibar's Swahili-Arab culinary heritage.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for Tanzania?
faq.a: Yes, most nationalities need a visa, best arranged as an e-visa in advance (about $50 for most nationalities; US citizens specifically need the $100 multiple-entry visa).

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Kilimanjaro International (JRO) for the safari circuit; Zanzibar (ZNZ) has its own airport for the coastal leg.

faq.q: Does the e-visa cover Zanzibar too?
faq.a: Yes, a single Tanzania e-visa covers both the mainland and Zanzibar — no separate permit needed.

faq.q: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination?
faq.a: Only if arriving from a country where yellow fever is endemic, or transiting more than 12 hours through one — otherwise not required.

daysReason: 9 days covers the northern safari circuit (Tarangire, Lake Manyara, Ngorongoro, Serengeti) plus Zanzibar to unwind. 6 works if you skip Zanzibar; 12+ lets you slow the safari pace down or add the southern circuit.
visa: An e-Visa or visa on arrival is available for most nationalities — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Serengeti
attractions.desc: As planícies abertas do Serengeti acolhem a maior migração de mamíferos terrestres da Terra, com mais de um milhão de gnus e zebras num circuito constante entre a Tanzânia e o Quénia. Os safaris fotográficos aqui contam-se entre os mais fiáveis do mundo para avistar leões, chitas e leopardos. A escala da paisagem, plana e com um horizonte amplo, faz parte da experiência em si.

attractions.name: Monte Kilimanjaro
attractions.desc: O pico mais alto de África eleva-se sozinho a partir das planícies circundantes, com o seu cume nevado visível a grandes distâncias apesar de estar quase sobre o equador. Várias rotas de vários dias sobem através de cinco zonas ecológicas distintas antes de alcançar o Pico Uhuru. Não é necessária experiência de escalada técnica, mas a altitude torna a etapa final genuinamente exigente.

attractions.name: Cratera do Ngorongoro
attractions.desc: Uma caldeira vulcânica colapsada forma um recinto natural repleto de vida selvagem, incluindo uma das poucas populações remanescentes de rinocerontes negros na região. O chão da cratera mantém-se verde mesmo na época seca, atraindo animais das terras altas. Descer as paredes da cratera de veículo dá a sensação de entrar num ecossistema autónomo.

attractions.name: Stone Town, Zanzibar
attractions.desc: Este antigo porto comercial na ilha de Zanzibar mistura arquitetura árabe, persa, indiana e europeia ao longo de ruas estreitas e sombreadas. Portas de madeira esculpidas e mercados de especiarias recordam séculos como polo do comércio no Oceano Índico. Combina naturalmente com as praias de areia branca noutras zonas da ilha.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional de Tarangire
attractions.desc: Conhecido pela sua paisagem pontilhada de baobás e grandes manadas de elefantes que se juntam ao longo do Rio Tarangire na época seca. É mais tranquilo que o Serengeti mas continua a oferecer avistamentos densos de vida selvagem, particularmente elefantes e aves. Muitos itinerários incluem-no como paragem mais curta antes ou depois dos parques maiores.

attractions.name: Lago Manyara
attractions.desc: Um parque compacto situado sob a escarpa do Rift, conhecido pelos leões que sobem às árvores e por grandes bandos de flamingos junto à margem do lago alcalino. A densa floresta de água subterrânea dá lugar rapidamente à margem aberta do lago, concentrando paisagens variadas numa área pequena. É frequentemente visitado como aquecimento antes do Serengeti.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–2
itinerary.title: Arusha e Tarangire
itinerary.desc: Aclimata-te em Arusha antes de um primeiro safári entre os baobás e manadas de elefantes de Tarangire.

itinerary.label: Dia 3
itinerary.title: Lago Manyara
itinerary.desc: Uma visita mais curta ao parque conhecido pelos leões que sobem às árvores e bandos de flamingos.

itinerary.label: Dias 4–5
itinerary.title: Cratera do Ngorongoro
itinerary.desc: Desce à cratera para uma observação densa de vida selvagem num ecossistema autónomo.
itinerary.logistics: ~1,5h de carro desde o Lago Manyara

itinerary.label: Dias 6–7
itinerary.title: Serengeti
itinerary.desc: Safaris prolongados pelas planícies, coordenados com a migração se possível.

itinerary.label: Dias 8–9
itinerary.title: Zanzibar
itinerary.desc: Voa até à costa para a Stone Town e praia, para fechar a viagem.

goodToKnow.tipping: 15–20 USD/dia para guias e motoristas de safari é habitual
goodToKnow.safety: Os safaris são bem organizados através de operadores estabelecidos; a Stone Town de Zanzibar é segura para andar de dia
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Transferências de avioneta ligam rapidamente os parques do circuito norte; as estradas entre eles são longas e difíceis
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) is the main gateway for the northern safari circuit; Zanzibar has its own airport (ZNZ) for the coastal leg

food.name: Ugali
food.desc: Uma papa firme de milho que forma a base amilácea da maioria das refeições diárias tanzanianas.

food.name: Nyama choma
food.desc: Carne grelhada no carvão, normalmente cabra ou vaca, um pilar da alimentação social casual.

food.name: Pizza de Zanzibar
food.desc: Uma especialidade de rua da Stone Town: uma massa fina recheada com carne, ovo e legumes, depois frita.

food.name: Pilau
food.desc: Arroz especiado cozinhado com carne e especiarias quentes, mostrando a herança culinária suaíli-árabe de Zanzibar.
